significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive relation: “tracing peaks systematically fail to coincide with best-edit layers,” while a fact-specific layer-leverage measure predicts edit success across model families, relations, and editing methods. This would constrain future edit-location decisions and interpretations of localization evidence because ROME (Meng et al., 2022) uses causal tracing to motivate where factual associations are edited, while Hase et al. (2023), “Does Localization Inform Editing?”, identifies the tracing–editability mismatch as a consequential methodological issue. It establishes a weighty cross-setting phenomenon and a practical predictive coupling, but only a tentative mechanism—“localization for reading differs from localization for writing”—and the unspecified claim that variation occurs “in predictable ways” weakens precision; the negative branch would nevertheless support tracing peaks as reliable edit selectors and reject the proposed read/write dissociation. The topic-substitution check passes: replacing these specific comparative relations with the generic topic of knowledge representation would not justify this score, because the added value comes from settling which measurable localization signal predicts successful intervention.

reach.justification: The named handle is a “direct edit-efficacy predictor: a cheap forward-backward probe estimating each layer’s leverage on the output for the specific fact,” used to select an edit location. It is ex ante because it ranks layers before an edit is committed, giving knowledge-editing researchers and model maintainers an action window to improve success and specificity rather than merely explaining a completed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted conclusion still predicts a relation—that higher probe leverage selects better locations than tracing peaks—and its stated scope spans “multiple model families, relations, and editing methods,” although acknowledged method dependence prevents treating it as architecture-independent. The topic-substitution check passes: the broad knowledge-retrieval topic alone supplies neither this selector nor its lead time, transferable comparison, or prospective use in updating deployed models.
